figures.alt: Investor involvement and company organization appear as separate sets of choices connected by an agreed blueprint.
The board agrees the plan and reviews it with company leaders, who make delivery decisions and allocate funded product and engineering capacity.
An operating adviser contributes judgment under an agreed remit; a company leader makes the decision and the company team supplies implementation capacity.
Shared specialists have competing requests; a named assignment agrees people, dates and cost with an assignment owner inside the company, whose local team implements and operates the result.

An illustrative program leader reports to the CEO and works with assigned people inside the company, with scope, budget and a planned handover to a permanent owner; investor review runs through the CEO.
Four equal panels pair a decision route with board oversight, experienced judgment with an adviser, specialist skill with shared experts, and execution capacity with dedicated company work.
In the fictional identity pilot, a specialist works for six weeks and a program leader for twelve; the week-six review narrows rollout, while week twelve leaves the assignment’s continuation open.
